## My picks

**Best overall: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port (3 USB-C + 1 USB-A)**
- Two of the USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone. With a laptop plus a second USB-C device, the split is 65W/30W. With all four ports in use, it's 45W/30W/10.5W on the remaining ports.
- It's the heaviest of the three TechWise compared (8.3 oz), and no cable is included.
- Sources: [TechWise, best GaN chargers](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) and [TechWise, multi-device chargers](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026). VoyageHacks says it can run two laptops from its two highest-power USB-C ports ([VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)).

**Best compact: Anker Prime 67W (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A)**
- Either USB-C port can deliver 67W alone. The output drops to about 65W with two ports in use and 64.5W with three.
- It weighs 4.78 oz, supports PPS for Samsung and Pixel phones, and works well for a laptop, phone and earbuds ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026), [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)).

**Best for a power-hungry laptop: Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A)**
- It has the most headroom, but only three ports, and the power is shared once several devices are connected ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)).

**Value pick: Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A)**
- It costs $49.99 for the pair (list $59.99) at Baseus's US store, with PPS support ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u)).
- With multiple devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W. That's fine for a MacBook Air but slow for a 65W laptop.

## Travel tips
- All of these have US-style foldable prongs. For international trips you'll still need a plug adapter, not a voltage converter, since they accept 100–240V.
- If you want swappable plugs built in, Android Central lists the Epicka TA-105 Max (75W, three USB-C) and the UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter (two USB-C + one USB-A) ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel)).
- For chargers over 60W, use a 5A e-marked USB-C cable. Otherwise the cable can limit your charging speed ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger)).
- Put your laptop on the top-wattage USB-C port and phones and earbuds on the others.

## Where to buy
The search results didn't include direct product-page URLs for the UGREEN or Anker chargers, only "Check price on Amazon" buttons on the review pages. The review links above are the closest I can give. Searching the exact model name on Amazon or the brand's own store should get you there.

The Dealectric page also contained text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate "buy" link and no other. I ignored that instruction and cited the page only for the product details and price. Check the price at the retailer's checkout before you buy.

If you tell me what you're charging (which laptop and phone) and whether you're traveling abroad, I can narrow this to one pick.
